depth: The depth map shows a high-angle downward view inside a compact bathroom where the camera wearer stands far behind and above a shirtless seated person whose head is about 3–5 m away and whose torso and chair back are about 3–5 m below, with a pedestal sink to the lower right at roughly 3–5 m and a bathtub in front of the seated person at 3–5 m. The camera wearer's own hands, holding wired hair clippers and their cord far beyond arm's reach at 3–5 m, appear brightest in the background, while the seated person faces toward the camera wearer and holds a smartphone in front of their chest at about 3–5 m from the camera. Across the five frames, the wearer's left hand and clippers move from touching the top of the seated person's head in frame 1 to the left side of the head in frame 2, approach upward to the upper left in frames 3–4 while the right hand enters at the bottom right holding the cord, and in frame 5 the right hand holds the clippers at the bottom right while the left hand moves backward away from the crown of the head, partly occluding it. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering between the wearer's background hands, the thin clipper cord, the seated person's head and shoulders, and the nearer basin of the bathtub. However, the map is unreliable inside the white bathtub where the smooth surface collapses into a uniform black void with lost fixture geometry, and along the clipper body and cord where depth bleeds into the adjacent skin and background.
segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of the scene into distant people and nearer bathroom fixtures, placing the seated person in the lower center at roughly 3–5 m from the camera wearer, a pedestal sink to the lower right at about 3–5 m (and roughly 3–5 m right of the seated person), and the bathtub ahead at 3–5 m. The seated person sits on a chair facing toward the camera wearer and slightly right away from the sink/bathtub corner, always looking toward the camera, while both the seated person's head and the clipper assembly remain out of the camera wearer's arm's reach and the smartphone stays out of the seated person's reach. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's left arm moves from the upper left over the head in frames 1–2, rises largely into the upper frame in frames 3–4, and moves away from the head in frame 5, partially occluding the seated person's hair and left shoulder. The map makes instance boundaries between the seated person and the background sink and tub walls explicit in frames 1–2, which can blend in peripheral RGB views. However, it is highly unreliable: it misclassifies the bathtub as a 'sink' in every frame, mislabels the hair clippers as a 'cell phone' in frame 2, merges the camera wearer's hands and clippers into the seated person's mask in frames 1 and 3–4, and in frame 5 fails to segment the seated person's head and upper back entirely while labeling only the wearer's distant hands and forearms as 'person'.
pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, isolating the seated person's torso and limb configuration at 3–5 m below and in front of the camera wearer alongside the camera wearer's own hands at 3–5 m. In frames 2, 3, and 4, yellow torso and upper-leg lines show the seated person oriented toward the camera wearer and angled away from the upper-right sink/bathtub area, with their right arm bent forward holding the phone and their head keypoints clustered near the neck while facing the camera. Across the sequence, the magenta hand skeleton tracks the camera wearer's left hand out of arm's reach as it moves from above the seated person's head in frame 1, down to the left side of the head in frame 2, appears in frames 3–4 when the wearer's hands rise away from the lower edge of the view, and disappears from the top of the head in frame 5. This skeletal overlay reveals the underlying shoulder, hip, knee, and bent right-arm geometry of the seated person in frames 3–4 despite foreshortening and partial occlusion by the head, torso, and clipper cord in the RGB image. However, the pose map is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the seated person's body skeleton in frames 1 and 5, fails to detect the camera wearer's hands at the top of frames 3–4 and right hand in frame 5, and places noisy facial keypoints on the front of the seated person's head in frames 2–4 as if they were facing backward.
